headline: Sr. Software Engineer | Design Systems, Accessibility & AI

experiences.titleOverride: Sr. Fullstack Engineer, Design Systems & Accessibility Lead

bullets.text: Engineer reusable React and TypeScript components with a built-in accessibility contract, so product teams inherit WCAG conformance and ship fewer accessibility bugs.
Prototype and wireframe new features alongside designers, and set them up to prototype on their own with real design-system components using AI tooling.
Cut accessibility violations in new pull requests 80% over six months with AI review agents.
Cut re-renders over 85% while AI chat responses stream by restructuring state ownership and narrowing Zustand store subscriptions.
Drove a company-critical accessibility initiative across 6 teams, closing 480 WCAG 2.1 issues and delivering SchoolAI's first VPAT, which unlocked major higher-ed and statewide deals.
Made the design system consumable by AI coding agents, building skills that translate designs into code and code into designs while following established engineering patterns and standards.
Ship multiplied output with agentic coding tools such as Claude Code and Codex, validating, refactoring, and taking accountability for AI-generated code without compromising fidelity.
Built a real-time AI analysis layer over 17k+ daily student chats that gives teachers insights, sentiment, progress scoring, and alerts for concerning content.
Developed the React frontend for Lucid's integration marketplace, driving 14 new partner-built integrations and 540,000+ installs in its first year.
Built modular, performant React and TypeScript components aligned to brand standards via Styled Components, contributing to Lucid's internal design system.
Built tooling to track Core Web Vitals across Lucid's marketing site over time.
Optimized caching and static generation so Lucid's marketing sites stayed fast under high traffic.
Led a team of engineers, mentoring through regular 1:1s, targeted feedback, and code review.
Rebuilt canyonsdistrict.org from scratch, cutting average page load times 20%.
Architected a permissions allocation system with site-wide activity auditing and improved LDAP authentication, strengthening security and operational visibility.

body: The work I'm proudest of has helped people who could easily have been left out. That's what pulled me into education, and then into accessibility. Amazon Leo's mission to close the digital divide makes the same promise accessibility does, that the web should work for everyone, not just the people who are easiest to reach.

Leo gets to set its quality bar from day one, and I've learned that the bar has to live in the system, not in heroics. At SchoolAI, I drove an accessibility initiative across six teams that closed 480 WCAG 2.1 issues and led to delivery of our first VPAT, unblocking deals with universities and states. Closing issues wasn't enough, though, because every new feature was a chance for the same problems to come back. So we built quality into the foundation. Our design-system components carry their own accessibility contract, shared form validation makes the accessible path the default, and AI review agents flag problems before code merges. Over six months, accessibility violations in new pull requests fell 80% as engineers internalized the patterns.

Amazon's principle to "insist on the highest standards," paired with this role's call to ship quickly and iterate often, is the balance I care about most. Generative AI has multiplied what we can deliver, but I take accountability for every line I ship. The quality bar doesn't move.
Leo's customers are the people the internet has left out the longest. I want to build the site that finally lets them in.
coverLetter.signoff: Thank you for your time & consideration,
